mainTopic: Things that block a כהן from the floor, loose floor stones, and רבי שמעון's view that collecting blood with the left hand is valid
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. When two verses state the same death penalty, we cannot extend it to other cases. Even according to the opinion that two verses can teach, the verse about שתויי יין makes three, and everyone agrees three cannot teach. Next, the גמרא learns from the school of רבי ישמעאל that a כהן standing on vessels, an animal, or another person's feet is פסול. The floor makes him fit to serve just like his garments do, so nothing may block between him and the floor. The גמרא explains why the משנה needed all three examples. It then brings רבי אליעזר's test for a כהן with one foot on the floor and one on a vessel or stone. After that come רבי אמי's questions about a loose or missing floor stone, which end in a תיקו. Finally, the גמרא turns to collecting blood with the left hand. רבי שמעון rules it valid, and the גמרא works hard to explain his reasoning: רב יהודה's answer is rejected, רבא's answer is challenged by רב סמא, and אביי begins a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two verses that say the same thing cannot teach other cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the rule that when two verses teach the same law, we cannot learn from them to other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion. It explains why we cannot take the death penalty stated in two verses and apply it to other similar cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if a law appears in one place, we might try to apply it to similar cases. But if the Torah had to write the same law twice, that suggests the law applies only to those cases. If it were a general rule, one verse would have been enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that come as one: two separate verses that teach the same law
They do not teach: we cannot learn from them to other cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of how we learn from verses, and it appears all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: And any two verses
that come as one
phrases.notes: Meaning two verses that both state the same law.

phrases.english: do not teach.
phrases.notes: They can't be used to extend the death penalty to other cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous section about extending the death penalty to other cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule of learning from verses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have extended the death penalty from the verses that state it to other similar cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since two verses state the same law, they do not teach other cases.

steps.title: Even the lenient opinion agrees, because there are three verses
steps.stepSummary: Even according to the opinion that two verses can teach, the verse about שתויי יין is a third verse, and everyone agrees three verses cannot teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says they do teach: those who drank wine are a third verse, and everyone agrees that three verses do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes sure its answer works for everyone, including the opinion that two verses can teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that two verses can teach other cases. But the death penalty also appears in the verse about a כהן who drank wine, so we have three verses. Everyone agrees that three verses repeating the same law cannot be applied to other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
כהנים who drank wine before doing the עבודה
According to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: Two verses teaching the same law: there is a dispute whether they can teach other cases. Three verses: everyone agrees they cannot.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says they do teach –
those who drank wine are a third,
phrases.notes: The verse about a כהן who drank wine also says he gets death, so it's a third verse with the same law.

phrases.english: and three, according to everyone,
do not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the answer of step 1 work for the other opinion as well.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Covers the opposing opinion by adding a third verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the opinion that two verses can teach, maybe we could extend the death penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: שתויי יין makes three verses, and three verses never teach, even according to that opinion.

steps.title: A כהן standing on something is פסול: what is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a כהן standing on vessels, an animal, or another person's feet is פסול, and asks where we learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Standing on vessels, on an animal, or on another person's feet makes him פסול. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a כהן doing the עבודה is פסול if he is standing on something instead of directly on the floor. The Torah does not clearly say this anywhere, so the גמרא asks how we know it.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of
Unfit: the עבודה he does is not valid
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: One standing on vessels,
on an animal,
on the feet of his fellow – is unfit.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the verses discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a כהן may not have anything between his feet and the floor.

steps.title: The floor is like the priestly garments: nothing may block
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that the floor makes the כהן holy just like the בגדי כהונה do. Since nothing may block between him and his garments, nothing may block between him and the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: since the floor makes holy and the service vessels make holy, just as nothing may separate between him and the service vessels, so too nothing may separate between him and the floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that compares the floor to the בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the floor of the עזרה and the בגדי כהונה make the כהן fit to serve. We already know nothing may come between the כהן's body and his garments. So the same must be true for the floor: if something blocks between his feet and the floor, it is a חציצה and he is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The floor of the עזרה
Makes holy: makes the כהן fit to serve
Service vessels: here, the בגדי כהונה
Blocks, separates: something that comes between
The school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: Here כלי שרת does not mean the regular vessels like bowls. It means the בגדי כהונה, which also make the כהן fit to serve.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that a כהן's feet must touch the floor directly during the עבודה.

phrases.english: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Since the floor sanctifies
and service vessels sanctify;
phrases.notes: Here 'service vessels' means the בגדי כהונה the כהן wears.

phrases.english: just as with service vessels –
nothing may interpose
between him and the service vessels,
so too with the floor –
nothing may interpose
between him and the floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison: the floor makes the כהן holy like his garments do, so nothing may block between him and the floor, just as nothing may block between him and his garments.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed all three examples
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each of the משנה's three examples teaches something new: a vessel is not flesh, an animal is flesh but not human, and another person's feet are human.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary. If it had taught us only a vessel, that would be because it is not a type of flesh, but an animal, which is flesh, I would say it does not block. And if it had taught us only an animal, that would be because it is not human, but his fellow, who is human, I would say it does not block. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה listed three examples instead of one. Each example blocks a mistake we might have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From a vessel alone, we might think only lifeless objects block, but an animal's body does not. From an animal alone, we might think only non-humans block, but another person, who is like the כהן, does not. So the משנה lists all three to show that anything between the כהן's feet and the floor makes him פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: each case teaches something new
If it had taught us only
A type of flesh
I would say no: I would have thought the rule does not apply

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן must stand directly on the floor of the עזרה. Anything in between, whether a vessel, an animal, or even another person's feet, is a חציצה and makes him פסול.

phrases.english: And it is necessary;
phrases.notes: Meaning all three examples in the משנה are needed.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us a vessel –
that is because they are not a type of flesh;
but an animal, which is a type of flesh –
I would say not.
phrases.notes: I would have thought an animal does not count as blocking.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us an animal –
that is because it is not of the human kind;
but his fellow, who is a human –
I would say not;
so it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה quoted in step 3 needed to list three separate examples.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One example would be enough; or an animal or a person, being flesh or human, would not count as blocking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each example is needed to show that even flesh, and even a fellow human, blocks the כהן from the floor.

steps.title: One foot on a vessel or stone, one foot on the floor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that when one foot is on a vessel or stone and the other on the floor, we check whether the כהן could stand on the floor foot alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, if a כהן has one foot on a vessel and one on the floor, or one foot on a stone and one on the floor, we look at the situation. If he could still stand on one foot and serve once the vessel or stone was taken away, his service is valid. If not, his service is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that deals with a mixed case: only one foot is blocked from the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 dealt with a כהן standing fully on something that blocks him from the floor. Here only one foot is blocked. The test is whether the floor foot alone could carry him: if it could, the other foot is treated as extra and does not count as a block.

keyTerms.meaning: The floor of the עזרה
We look at the case and judge it
His Temple service is valid
His Temple service is invalid

steps.whatToRemember: The test is: take away the vessel or stone. Could he still stand and serve on the floor foot alone? If yes, his service is כשר. If no, it is פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next questions about stones. If a stone counts as a separate object, it can be a block between the כהן and the floor.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If one of his feet was on a vessel
and one of his feet was on the floor,
or one of his feet was on a stone
and one of his feet was on the floor, we look:
phrases.notes: He means a loose stone lying on the floor, not one of the floor's own stones.

phrases.english: In any case where, if the vessel were taken away
or the stone were taken away,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד עַל רַגְלוֹ אַחַת וְיַעֲבוֹד –
phrases.english: he could stand on his one foot and serve,
his service is valid;
and if not, his service is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a mixed case to the rule against anything coming between the כהן and the floor: only one foot is blocked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the כהן could stand and serve on the floor foot alone, his service is valid. If not, it is invalid.

steps.title: A loose floor stone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks: if a floor stone came loose and the כהן stood on it, is that a block between him and the floor?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי asked: if a floor stone came loose and the כהן stood on it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי raises a new question. The גמרא will narrow it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loose stone is still part of the floor, but it is no longer firmly attached. The question is whether it still counts as floor, or as a separate object that blocks the כהן from the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that may not have a clear answer
It came loose and became wobbly
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami asked:
If the stone came loose
and he stood on it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "He" is the כהן doing the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the blocking rule to a new case: a floor stone that is half attached.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a loose floor stone counts as part of the floor or as something that blocks the כהן from the floor.

steps.title: Narrowing the question: he plans to reattach it
steps.stepSummary: If there is no plan to fix the stone, it certainly blocks. The real question is when he plans to reattach it: does that plan make it count as attached already?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not plan to reattach the stone, there is no question: it certainly blocks. The question is only when he plans to reattach it. What is the law then? Since he plans to reattach it, is it treated as if it were already attached? Or perhaps, right now at least, it is detached?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where רבי אמי's question applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one will fix the stone, it is simply a separate object and it blocks. The open question is whether a plan to reattach it makes it count as attached now, or whether only its present state matters.

keyTerms.meaning: He plans to reattach it
It blocks; it is a חציצה between the כהן and the floor
Detached
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the loose stone always blocks. When there is no plan to fix it, it blocks for sure. The question is only about a stone that will be reattached.

phrases.english: Where he does not plan to reattach it,
do not ask, since it certainly blocks.
Where you should ask is when he plans to reattach it.
What is the law? Since he plans to reattach it,
is it like something that is attached?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא הָא תְּלִישָׁא?
phrases.english: Or perhaps, right now at least, it is detached?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לְחַבְּרָהּ לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי אמי's question to the one case that is really in doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a plan to reattach the stone makes it count as attached already, so that it does not block.

steps.title: Another version: standing where a stone was removed
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטי reports רבי אמי's question differently: the stone was pulled out, and the כהן stood in the empty spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטי reports the question this way: רבי אמי asked, if the stone was pulled out and the כהן stood in its place, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי אמי's question. In this version nothing is under the כהן's foot. He stands on the ground where the stone used to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version there is no object at all between the כהן and the ground. The question becomes whether the ground under the floor stones is also holy floor.

keyTerms.meaning: He reports the question this way
It was pulled out
In its place

phrases.english: Rabba Zuti asks it this way:
Rabbi Ami asked:
If the stone was pulled out
and he stood in its place, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי אמי's question from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן standing on the bare ground under a removed floor stone counts as standing on the holy floor.

steps.title: How deep did דוד's holiness go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question is whether דוד sanctified only the top floor level, or all the way down into the depths.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is his question? When דוד sanctified the place, did he sanctify only the upper floor? Or perhaps he sanctified it all the way down to the bottom of the depths?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind רבי אמי's second version and suggests an answer. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the top surface was made holy, the ground under a missing stone is not holy floor. If the holiness reaches all the way down, the כהן is still standing on holy ground.

keyTerms.meaning: What exactly is he asking?
He made it holy
The upper (top) floor level
The bottom of the depths

phrases.english: What is he asking?
When David sanctified,
phrases.notes: This refers to דוד המלך setting aside the site of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: did he sanctify only the upper floor?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא עַד לְאַרְעִית תְּהוֹמָא קַדֵּישׁ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps he sanctified down to the bottom of the depths?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the idea behind רבה זוטי's version of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What idea makes the removed-stone case a real question.

steps.title: Then why not ask about the whole courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: If the question is about how deep the holiness goes, it should be asked about the whole courtyard floor, not just one missing stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let him ask about the entire courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just suggested in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the question is how deep דוד's holiness went, that question applies to the entire floor of the עזרה. So why would רבי אמי ask only about the spot of one missing stone? This suggests step 10's explanation does not fit the narrow way the question was asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him ask
The Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Then let him ask about the entire courtyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's explanation of the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי אמי is asking how deep דוד's sanctification went.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the issue, it would apply to the whole courtyard floor. So it is strange to ask only about the spot of one missing stone.

steps.title: The real question is whether this is a normal way to serve
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. רבי אמי was sure the holiness goes all the way down. He was really asking whether standing in a gap in the floor counts as a proper way to do the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he was sure that the holiness goes down to the deepest depths. What he was asking is this: is standing like this a normal way of serving, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11 by explaining that רבי אמי's question was never about how deep the holiness goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked why the question would focus on one missing stone if it were about depth. The answer is that depth is not in doubt. The doubt is whether a כהן standing in a hole in the floor is serving in the normal, proper manner. That issue only comes up with a single missing stone, so the challenge is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (it is just as we said, only explained differently)
The very bottom of the depths
A normal, proper way of doing the עבודה
He is asking / his question is

phrases.english: Actually, it is obvious to him
that he sanctified it down to the bottom of the depths;
and this is what he is asking:
is this a normal way of serving,
or is this not a normal way of serving?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּעַד אַרְעִית תְּהוֹמָא קַדֵּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by changing what the question is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was whether the holiness goes all the way down
steps.terutzMaskana: The depth is certain. The question is whether standing in a gap counts as proper service.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבי אמי's question without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying the question cannot be settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found to decide whether standing in the gap is a proper way to serve. So the question is left open, and this closes the section about the floor stone.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's question ends up being about proper manner of service (דרך שירות), not depth of holiness. It is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question as reframed in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether standing in a gap in the floor is proper service remains undecided.

steps.title: The משנה: collecting blood with the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. If the כהן collected the blood with his left hand, it is invalid, but רבי שמעון says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he collected the blood with his left hand, it is invalid, and רבי שמעון says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, setting up a discussion about using the left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. The תנא קמא and רבי שמעון argue about whether קבלה done with the left hand is valid. The next steps look for the source of each view.

keyTerms.meaning: He collected (the blood in a vessel)
Left hand
Rules it valid

phrases.english: If he collected with the left hand, it is invalid,
and רבי שמעון rules it valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִיבֵּל בִּשְׂמֹאל פָּסוּל וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: quotes the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קבלה with the left hand is invalid according to the תנא קמא, and valid according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The source that collecting and placing need the right hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'with his finger' as connected to both 'and he shall take' and 'and he shall put.' So both collecting and placing must be done with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'with his finger' and 'he shall take' teaches that collecting may only be done with the right hand. 'With his finger and he shall put' teaches that placing may only be done with the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the first opinion in the משנה: the left hand is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'he shall take... with his finger, and put.' The ברייתא links the word 'finger,' which means the right hand, both to 'take' (collecting) and to 'put' (placing). So both acts need the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: With his finger
Collecting the blood
Placing the blood on the מזבח
Right hand

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not find the word 'right' in this פסוק. It learns 'right hand' from the word 'finger.' The next steps depend on this point.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'With his finger' and 'and he shall take'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25. The ברייתא reads 'with his finger' as going with 'take' too, not only with 'put.'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַבָּלָה אֶלָּא בְּיָמִין.
phrases.english: teaches that collecting may only be done with the right hand.
'With his finger and he shall put'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא נְתִינָה אֶלָּא בְּיָמִין.
phrases.english: teaches that placing may only be done with the right hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first opinion of the משנה
steps.raayaObject: Collecting with the left hand is invalid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'he shall take with his finger and put' (ויקרא 4:25)

steps.title: רבי שמעון: no hand is mentioned for collecting
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the word 'finger' only goes with placing. Since no hand is mentioned for collecting, collecting with the left hand is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Is 'hand' mentioned regarding collecting? Rather, 'with his finger and he shall put' means only placing must be with the right hand. Since 'hand' is not mentioned with collecting, if he collected with the left it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון rejects the ברייתא's reading for collecting and gives the source for his own view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees that placing needs the right hand. But he reads 'with his finger' as attached only to 'and he shall put.' For collecting, no hand is mentioned at all, so there is no right-hand requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Was it then said...? (a challenge: it was not said)
Hand (any mention of the hand or finger)
Since
Valid

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said:
Is 'hand' mentioned regarding collecting?!
Rather, 'with his finger and he shall put'
means that placing may only be done with the right hand;
since 'hand' is not mentioned regarding collecting,
if he collected with the left hand, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְכִי נֶאֶמְרָה יָד בְּקַבָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first half of the ברייתא's reading in step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the requirement for collecting. He agrees about placing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'With his finger' is attached only to 'put,' so nothing in the פסוק links a hand to collecting.

steps.title: Either way, רבי שמעון's reasoning seems not to work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. If he uses the גזירה שוה, the word 'finger' already appears, so why care that 'hand' is missing? If he does not use it, mentioning 'hand' would not require the right hand anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for רבי שמעון, whichever way you take it: if he accepts the גזירה שוה, so what if 'hand' is not mentioned with collecting? And if he does not accept the גזירה שוה, so what if 'hand' were mentioned with collecting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's reasoning by showing it fails under both possible views about the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that 'finger' or 'hand' means the right hand comes from a גזירה שוה. If רבי שמעון accepts it, the word 'finger' in the פסוק should be enough to require the right hand, even with no word 'hand' near collecting. If he rejects it, then even a word 'hand' would not mean 'right hand,' so his argument about whether 'hand' appears makes no difference either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it: an argument that fails under both options
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
What difference does it make?

phrases.english: And as for רבי שמעון, whichever way you take it:
if he accepts the גזירה שוה,
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה that teaches that 'hand' or 'finger' in these פסוקים means the right hand.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה יָד בְּקַבָּלָה מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: so what if 'hand' is not mentioned regarding collecting?
And if he does not accept the גזירה שוה,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נֶאֶמְרָה יָד בְּקַבָּלָה מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: so what if 'hand' were mentioned regarding collecting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning רבי שמעון gave in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's argument that collecting is valid with the left hand because 'hand' is not mentioned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: with the גזירה שוה, the missing word 'hand' does not matter. Without it, the word 'hand' would not matter either. So his argument decides nothing.

steps.title: רב יהודה: רבי שמעון does not accept the verbal analogy
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers the challenge from step 17. He says רבי שמעון does not use the גזירה שוה, and what he means is that the words 'right hand' never appear for collecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Really, רבי שמעון does not accept the גזירה שוה. This is what he means: Does the Torah say 'right hand' about collecting? Since it does not say 'right hand' about collecting, if the כהן collected with his left hand, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from step 17 by choosing one side of it. He says רבי שמעון does not use the גזירה שוה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 asked: with the גזירה שוה, why care that 'hand' is missing, and without it, why would 'hand' matter? רב יהודה changes how we read רבי שמעון. He does not mean just the word 'hand.' He means the full words 'right hand,' which would clearly require the right hand even without any גזירה שוה. Since those words are not written about collecting, the left hand is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to one position firmly
He does not hold / does not accept
A teaching that links two places in the Torah through a shared word
Collecting the blood of the קרבן in a bowl
Since / because
Valid / fit

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Really, he does not hold of the verbal analogy;
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה from step 17, which teaches that 'hand' or 'finger' in the Torah means the right one.

phrases.english: and this is what he is saying:
But is 'right hand' stated about collecting?!

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר יַד יָמִין בְּקַבָּלָה,
phrases.english: Since 'right hand' is not stated about collecting,
if he collected with the left, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לְעוֹלָם לֵית לֵיהּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 17 by choosing the side where רבי שמעון rejects the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading רבי שמעון's words: 'hand' means the explicit words 'right hand.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's argument seemed meaningless whether or not he holds the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון rejects the גזירה שוה and only requires the right hand where the Torah explicitly says 'right hand.' It never says so for collecting.

steps.title: רבה: Then placing should also be valid with the left hand
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב יהודה. If only the explicit words 'right hand' count, then placing the blood should also be valid with the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: If so, then placing the blood should also be valid with the left hand!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב יהודה's answer. He says it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'right hand' are not written about placing the blood either. Only 'finger' is written there. So if רבי שמעון rejects the גזירה שוה, nothing would require the right hand for placing. Yet everyone, רבי שמעון included, agrees that placing needs the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Placing the blood on the מזבח
Also / too

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
If so,
even placing too!
phrases.notes: He means placing with the left would also be valid, since 'right hand' is not written there either, only 'finger.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ נְתִינָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that רבי שמעון rejects the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without the גזירה שוה, placing would also lack any source for the right hand. But רבי שמעון agrees that placing requires the right hand.

steps.title: רבה: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון does use the verbal analogy
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds a second challenge. A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון himself saying that every 'hand' and 'finger' in the Torah means the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides, does רבי שמעון really not accept the גזירה שוה? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: Wherever the Torah says 'hand,' it means only the right, and 'finger' means only the right!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה continues with a second attack on רב יהודה. He quotes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון clearly holds the rule about 'hand' and 'finger.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's whole answer depends on רבי שמעון rejecting the גזירה שוה. This ברייתא shows the opposite in רבי שמעון's own words: every 'hand' and every 'finger' means the right one. So רב יהודה's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds a second challenge
Every place / wherever
Finger

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's answer is rejected. רבי שמעון does hold that 'hand' and 'finger' in the Torah mean the right one.

phrases.english: And furthermore,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה?!
phrases.english: does Rabbi Shimon really not hold of the verbal analogy?!
But it was taught:
Rabbi Shimon says:
Every place where 'hand' is stated,
it means only the right;
'finger' means only the right!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, וְכִי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge from רבה against רב יהודה, adding to step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that רבי שמעון does not hold the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records רבי שמעון explicitly teaching that 'hand' and 'finger' always mean the right one.

steps.title: רבא: רבי שמעון uses the analogy, but 'finger' cannot mean collecting
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation. רבי שמעון does hold the גזירה שוה, but for collecting the Torah writes only 'finger,' and you cannot collect blood with a finger. So 'finger' must refer to placing, and collecting with the left hand is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Really, רבי שמעון does accept the גזירה שוה. This is what he means: Does the Torah say 'hand' about collecting? Since it does not say 'hand' about collecting, only 'finger,' and one cannot collect with a finger, if the כהן collected with his left hand, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב יהודה's answer fell, רבא offers a different answer. He takes the other side of step 17: רבי שמעון does hold the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that the word 'hand' itself is missing. Only 'finger' could connect to collecting, and collecting is not physically done with a finger. So 'finger' must belong only to placing, which then requires the right hand. Nothing in the פסוק requires the right hand for collecting.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the previous answer and starts a new one. Here also: 'but only'
He holds / accepts
It is impossible

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that 'hand' is needed to require the right hand. His point is that 'finger' cannot logically refer to collecting, so the right-hand rule that comes with 'finger' only applies to placing.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Really, he does hold of the verbal analogy;
and this is what he is saying:
But is 'hand' stated about collecting?!
Since 'hand' is not stated about collecting,
only 'finger,'
and it is impossible to collect with a finger;
if he collected with the left, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם אִית לֵיהּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יהודה's rejected answer with a new explanation that fits the ברייתא from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical limitation: the word 'finger' cannot apply to collecting, so it belongs only to placing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי שמעון holds the גזירה שוה, 'finger' in the פסוק should require the right hand for collecting too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Finger' cannot describe collecting, so it applies only to placing. Collecting has no right-hand requirement and is valid with the left.

steps.title: רב סמא: A bowl with a handle could be held with a finger
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי challenges רבא's answer. It is possible to collect with a finger if the bowl is made with a small handle on its rim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי said to רבינא: It is possible to make a small handle on the rim of the bowl and collect with it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא בריה דרב אשי attacks the key claim in רבא's answer, that one cannot collect blood with a finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's whole answer rests on 'it is impossible to collect with a finger.' רב סמא בריה דרב אשי shows a practical way to do it: put a small handle on the מזרק and hold it with one finger. If collecting with a finger is possible, 'finger' could refer to collecting after all, and רבא's answer is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible
Literally 'ear'; here, a small handle
The rim / edge of
The bowl used to collect the blood of a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Samma, son of Rav Ashi, said to Ravina:
It is possible that one makes
a handle on the rim of the bowl,
and collects with it!
phrases.notes: He means holding that little handle with one finger, so the blood really is collected 'with a finger.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא: אִיפְשָׁר דְּעָבֵיד לֵיהּ אֹזֶן לִשְׂפַת מִזְרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רבא's answer in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that it is impossible to collect with a finger
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bowl with a handle on its rim can be held with one finger, so collecting with a finger is possible. Then 'finger' could refer to collecting too.

steps.title: אביי begins a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: Since רבא's answer was challenged, the גמרא sets aside that approach and introduces אביי, who will offer a different explanation of רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is dropping רבא's answer and getting ready to give a new explanation from אביי, which begins on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means 'rather.' It tells us the previous answer did not hold up. רב סמא showed in step 22 that blood can be collected with a finger if the bowl has a small handle. So רבא's reason for why 'finger' cannot refer to collecting is gone, and a new explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is being dropped and a new one is coming.

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not contain אביי's answer yet. It only announces that he is about to give one. Don't look for his reasoning here.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 22 by setting aside רבא's explanation and opening a new one from אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer: the earlier explanation is dropped and a new source reading is about to be offered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought, following רבא, that 'finger' could not refer to collecting, so collecting with the left hand is valid according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reasoning failed because of the bowl with a handle. אביי will now give a different reason, which appears on the next amud.
